posts.text:
Two big updates to the $100K Hackathon 🏴‍☠️

1/ We have disqualified the #1 product.

After reviewing the entry, we found that work started before November 16 and that it was a reworked version of an existing product.

Both break the requirement to build a completely new business from zero after the hackathon starts.

This decision applies to the product. Jacky can still participate with a new business that meets the rules. The disqualified product’s revenue won’t carry over.

Here's the updated leaderboard: https://t.co/lZUe71oAFc

2/ We’re changing how the $100,000 is distributed.

I’ve been reading your feedback. Having one person win all the cash made the prize feel out of reach for many of you.

My goal with this hackathon is to get people to finally ship the business they’ve been thinking about. If more chances to win help more people keep going, that makes sense to me.

So we’re replacing the single $100K cash prize with:

🥇 1st: $30,000
🥈 2nd: $20,000
🥉 3rd: $10,000
4th: $8,000
5th: $7,000
6th: $5,000
7th: $5,000
8th: $5,000
9th: $5,000
10th: $5,000

Plus the iPhone Duo and MacBook Neo. 12 winners in total!

The cash pool stays at $100,000. Winners are still ranked by verified profit.

Building apps changed my life. I’m doing this with @jackfriks because I want more people to experience that too.

Thank you for helping us make this hackathon better 🫡

CHRIST THE KING COLLEGE, ONITSHA: CELEBRATING MY HERITAGE AND ENCOURAGING THE NEXT GENERATION 

Each year, my alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, invites me to its celebration of the Feast of Christ the King, scheduled for this Sunday, November 22. Although my demanding campaign schedule will prevent me from attending this year's ceremony, I made a brief visit to the school today while on my way to engage with traders and residents of Onitsha.

It was a warm and memorable visit, and I was graciously received by the School Administrator and Senior Prefect. In my interaction with the students, I emphasised the importance of education, urged them to remain focused and dedicated, and reminded them that Nigeria's future President could emerge from among them.

I also inspected the newly constructed Teachers' House, a project I facilitated with the support of friends to strengthen the school's teaching and learning environment.

CKC remains an enduring part of my life's journey, having shaped my values, discipline and sense of responsibility. I remain grateful for this lasting bond.
Wherever life takes us, the values of our alma mater remain with us. CKC will forever be home. -PO

I held a coordination call with the military and government officials. As of this morning, since last night, Russia has launched more than 400 attack drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic. The Russians spread this attack across many cities and regions of Ukraine. Absolutely all the targets were ordinary civilian infrastructure – things that literally sustain people’s lives. Energy facilities, logistics – bridges across the Dnipro, railway infrastructure. Strikes were also carried out, in particular, on substations and power lines that the nuclear power plants depend on and that connect Ukraine’s power grid with our neighbors in the European Union. Ordinary residential buildings were also damaged. Unfortunately, there are fatalities… At this point, we know that the strike killed eight people. My condolences to all their families and loved ones. Nearly 30 people have been injured. 

Restoration of energy facilities and infrastructure is already underway throughout Ukraine wherever the security situation allows. The Minister of Energy and government officials reported on all the details of the hits and the resources needed for restoration. The Russians also used missiles with cluster warheads. This was one of the largest attacks. The strike tactics were particularly vicious this time: several groups of missiles were launched, with pauses of 20–30 minutes between them, to make it harder to put out fires, clear rubble, and carry out repairs. People had essentially already been killed by the time specialists were inspecting the initial damage to the facilities, as the Russians were carrying out double-tap strikes. 

In total, 79 cruise missiles were shot down – and our warriors did an extremely professional job intercepting cruise missiles today. Our Ukrainian combat aviation performed very well – our F-16s, Mirages, and MiGs. Ballistic missiles are, unfortunately, much more difficult to deal with, and that depends not on our capabilities but on the supply of missiles by our partners. It is also worth separately recognizing our warriors who are trying to destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers using the means we have available. Tonight, we hit three launchers. One was destroyed, and we are still assessing the damage to the other two. 

There were also separate reports on the situation in Odesa and the region, Kyiv and the region, Sumy, Kharkiv and the region, the Dnipro region, and Ukraine’s western regions. Restoration deadlines have been set. 

We also need a clear response from the world to all this. It is important that our partners not only issue statements in support of Ukraine and Ukrainians, but also follow through on specific agreements on air defense. Putin launched this attack in a highly demonstrative manner – following weak meetings in China and the actual failure of his attempt to somehow “redraw” the world. And against the backdrop of Russia's positions on the front lines being at their weakest at any point this year. Russia is trying to compensate for its military and diplomatic impotence with precisely this kind of terror, precisely these attacks on life. 

I instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine to contact today each of the partners who have already begun preparing air defense packages. Deliveries need to be accelerated. I separately discussed with the Minister of Defense of Ukraine communication with our partners in the United States regarding the delivery of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles. We are counting very much on the Pentagon releasing the supplies we are waiting for. Glory to Ukraine!
